passage: In the garden in Bogota, Mateo carried a bag of soil to the pots. "Me! I can help!" Tomas, five, ran over with his arms out. "It's heavy," said Mateo. "I can!" Mateo nodded and handed him a small trowel. "Your job is filling the little pots, up to the line." Tomas scooped with his tongue out, soil on his nose. "Look, I did four!" He stood tall. "What's next?"

qa.q: What did Mateo hand Tomas?
qa.a: A small trowel.

qa.q: What does Tomas standing tall suggest?
qa.a: Pride in being capable and included. He may also want Mateo's praise.

qa.q: Why does giving Tomas a real task help?
qa.a: It lets him feel capable and included and builds a sense of responsibility.

qa.q: How might Mateo feel having a small helper?
qa.a: Probably pleased, though the work may go more slowly. He chose to hand over a real job.

grounding: Shows a young child volunteering with I can help and being given a small real task.

passage: At tidy-up time in the nursery, Parveen Ma'am asked who could help. "Me! I can help!" called Ujjwal, five, hand high. "Please put the blue blocks in the blue tub," she said. He crouched, sorted and counted under his breath. When he finished he tapped her arm. "Blue tub is full. Can I do the red ones?" She thanked him by name in front of the class, and Ujjwal looked around to see if his friends had heard.

qa.q: Which blocks did Ujjwal put in the blue tub?
qa.a: The blue blocks.

qa.q: Why did Ujjwal look around after being thanked?
qa.a: Likely to see whether his friends had noticed, showing he wants to feel capable and included. He may also just have been pleased.

qa.q: What could Parveen give Ujjwal next time?
qa.a: Another small real task, such as handing out cups or watering the class plant.

qa.q: How might a classmate who did not volunteer feel seeing Ujjwal thanked?
qa.a: Maybe a little left out, or maybe motivated to volunteer next time.

grounding: Shows a young child volunteering to help and being trusted with a real small job in a nursery.

passage: I'm Vidya, Afreen's big sister. Whenever Ammi cooks, Afreen runs in shouting, “Me! I can help!” Today Ammi was making sabzi. Instead of sending her out, Ammi gave her a bowl of tomatoes and said, “Wash these for me.” Afreen stood on the stool and washed every tomato, one by one, very seriously. Then she lined them up. “Done! What next?” Ammi gave her the peas to shell. I don't know if Afreen liked the work or just being with Ammi, but she was beaming.

qa.q: What did Ammi give Afreen to wash?
qa.a: A bowl of tomatoes.

qa.q: What might Afreen have been feeling as she washed the tomatoes?
qa.a: She seemed proud and happy to be included and useful. Vidya isn't sure if she enjoyed the work itself or being with Ammi.

qa.q: Why was giving Afreen a real task a good choice?
qa.a: It let her feel capable and included, and builds responsibility, instead of sending her out.

qa.q: How does Vidya see Afreen's eagerness?
qa.a: Vidya notices how serious and beaming Afreen is, and seems amused and fond.

grounding: A sister observes a preschooler volunteer to help cook, and their mother gives her small real tasks.

passage:
Saturday: Kunal was painting the balcony wall. Simran ran up. “I can help! Me!” “No, you'll make a mess,” he said. Simran sulked on the steps all afternoon.
Sunday: Simran asked again. This time Kunal gave her a small brush and pointed at the bottom corner. “This bit is yours.” She painted it very slowly, tongue out, and showed him every stroke.
Next Saturday: Simran came out in her old clothes. “Papa, what's my job today?” Kunal handed her the rag. “Wiping drips.” She wiped proudly.

qa.q: What did Kunal give Simran on Sunday?
qa.a: A small brush.

qa.q: What was Simran feeling when she sulked on the steps?
qa.a: She felt left out and disappointed at being told she'd make a mess when she wanted to help.

qa.q: What changed on Sunday, and why did it work?
qa.a: Kunal gave her a small, real task, the bottom corner, which let her feel capable and included.

qa.q: How might Kunal see Simran asking for her job the next Saturday?
qa.a: He likely feels pleased that she now takes her job seriously and wants to be responsible.

grounding: Over a week, a father learns to give his volunteering preschooler small real tasks instead of turning her away.

passage: Dark clouds were rolling in, and Usha Dadi had ten minutes to pack before the taxi came. Bhavna ran in. “Me! I can help!” Dadi almost said no. Instead she handed Bhavna a pile of socks. “Put these in the blue bag. Pairs together.” Bhavna knelt on the floor and matched them, whispering, “Pair, pair.” When the taxi honked, the socks were done. “I helped!” Bhavna told the driver. Dadi hugged her. “You did. I couldn't have done the socks in time.”

qa.q: Which bag did the socks go in?
qa.a: The blue bag.

qa.q: What was Bhavna feeling when she told the driver “I helped!”?
qa.a: She felt proud and capable, pleased that her job was done in time.

qa.q: Which choice by Dadi worked, and why?
qa.a: Even in a rush, she gave Bhavna a small, real task instead of saying no, so Bhavna felt included and useful.

qa.q: What would change if Dadi had told her to go away?
qa.a: Bhavna might have felt left out and hurt, and missed a chance to feel responsible.

grounding: In a rush before rain, a grandmother gives her volunteering granddaughter a small real task.

passage:
Gurleen came into the flat with four heavy bags from the market and dumped them on the floor.

"Me! I can help!" Vasudha came running, arms already out.

Gurleen almost said, "It's quicker if I do it." Then she looked at her daughter's shining face. "Okay. You're in charge of the bread. Put it in the bread tin."

Vasudha carried it in both hands, very slowly, and closed the lid with a bang. "Done! What next?"

"The bananas go in the basket."

By the end, Vasudha had put away six things. "I helped a lot," she told Papa.

qa.q: How many bags did Gurleen carry into the flat?
qa.a: Four heavy bags.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling when she said, "I helped a lot"?
qa.a: She was most likely proud and pleased to have done real jobs. Running in with her arms out shows she wanted to feel capable and included from the start.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: Gurleen gave Vasudha small real tasks, the bread and the bananas, instead of doing it all herself, which let Vasudha feel useful and responsible. 🙂

qa.q: How might Papa feel when Vasudha tells him she helped a lot?
qa.a: He would probably be pleased and proud, and his reaction could encourage her to volunteer again.

grounding: It shows a young child eagerly volunteering to help and small real tasks giving her a sense of responsibility.
